newsitem.title: USA: Judge declares mistrial in Kevorkian case.
newsitem.headline: Judge declares mistrial in Kevorkian case.

text.p: A judge declared a mistrial in Dr. Jack Kevorkian's fourth assisted suicide trial on Thursday, saying that inflammatory opening statements by defense attorney Geoffrey Fieger tainted the jury.

The decision by Ionia County Circuit Judge Charles Miel, coming only a day after the trial got under way, abruptly ended a small-town prosecutor's bid to convict the assisted suicide activist after three others have failed.

Miel said, however, that he believes Kevorkian can be re-tried on the same four felony charges without violation of double jeopardy laws that prohibit defendants from being tried twice for the same crime.
Fieger disagreed and said he would appeal any attempts to bring a new trial against Kevorkian all the way up to the U.S. Supreme Court.

In his ruling, Miel agreed with Prosecutor Raymond Voet's claim that several statements made by Fieger in his opening statement on Wednesday were improper, including personal attacks on Voet and assertions that evidence had been tampered with. It is highly unusual for a prosecutor to call for a mistrial.

"The extent of the possible bias cannot be measured, but the court feels there is a high likelihood that the impartiality of one or more of the jurors may be affected by the opening statement of defendant's council," Miel said. "Prejudice of the jury cannot be repaired by any corrective instructions."
